subject: Suspicious promo credit issuances — NebulaOps cohort
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Suspicious promo credit issuances — NebulaOps cohort

Hi Logan / Neha,

Our self-serve grants detector flagged a cluster of ~43 trial credit issuances tied to the NebulaOps org over the past 48 hours. Quick summary:
- 28 accounts share the same phone number P+1-555-0199 (formatted variants observed).
- 35 accounts registered from disposable or newly created domains (e.g. nebulalabs-mail[.]info, nebulaops-temp[.]online).
- Device signals show repeated rotation of user-agent strings and identical device fingerprint hashes for ~22 accounts.
- Several accounts consumed the initial free credit within minutes of issuance and started high-rate token usage.

Attached: suspect-signups-20270630.csv (account rows), device-fingerprint-samples.txt.

Recommendation: hold any further auto-approvals for NebulaOps, rollback credits for the clear duplicates, and require phone verification + org-backed email for remaining borderline accounts.

If Sales needs us to preserve a subset for an active deal we can carve exceptions but need explicit approval (deal id if applicable).

- Priyom
Priyom Das
Fraud Analytics, Redwood Inference

From: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 09:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Suspicious promo credit issuances — NebulaOps cohort

Thanks Priyom — that looks concerning.

Ben / Neha: NebulaOps is in active talks with Sales (see HubSpot deal DL-2027-0893). Before we take any public-facing action I need: 
- A short summary of which accounts are clearly fraudulent vs borderline (CSV row ids will do).
- Confirmation we can safely revoke credits without breaking an active demo for a named contact.

Priyom: if you can mark the 43 accounts and tag the 22 with identical fingerprints as "high confidence fraud" I authorize rollback for those. For the remaining borderline set, require phone MFA + company email verification before credits are reissued.

Please copy the legal/compliance guidance if rollback will touch paid invoices (I think this is all free credits). Marcus — can you confirm the rollback playbook & SLA for the customer-facing ticket?

- Logan
Logan Wright
Senior Account Exec, Redwood Inference

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Suspicious promo credit issuances — NebulaOps cohort

On Wed, Jun 30, 2027 at 9:35 AM Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com> wrote:
> Thanks Priyom — that looks concerning.

Attached CSV uses internal row ids. Quick mapping included inline:
- high_confidence_fraud: rows 3,7,11-18,22,23,29-36,40-43 (total 24)
- probable_duplicate_phone: rows 1,2,5,6,8,9,12,13,21 (phone reuse observed)
- borderline: rows 4,10,14,19,20,24-28,37-39

Device fingerprint sample (snippet):
- df_hash: a3f4c9... repeated 22 times across accounts, UA rotation pattern: Chrome/107 -> Brave/1.45 -> Edge/114 in rapid succession.
- IPs: bulk of signups from 3 ASN blocks with unusual geo distribution (US IPs but allocated to cheap/hosting ranges).

I recommend immediate rollback for the 24 high_confidence_fraud rows. For the probable_duplicate_phone group, we can require SMS OTP + org email. For borderline, hold credits pending manual review and outreach.

Attachments: suspect-signups-20270630.csv, device-fingerprint-samples.txt, nebulaops-account-sheet.pdf (manual notes from SDR contact).

If Sales wants to preserve specific account ids for active demos, list them now and we'll whitelist until you confirm.

- Priyom

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: ops@nebulaops.com
Cc: sales@nebulaops.com, Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 01 Jul 2027 08:17:00 -0700
Subject: Quick verification so we can keep your trial credits active

Hi NebulaOps team,

I'm Neha on the Redwood account team. We saw a cluster of new trial accounts tied to your org and want to confirm a few details so there is no interruption to your trial credits:
- Could you confirm a primary technical contact (name + direct mobile) for the demo?
- Please share a copy of a recent invoice or an org-level document (PDF) showing NebulaOps as the company behind these accounts.

If you prefer, we can also step through a quick screen-share with a product specialist to validate activity. We want to avoid accidentally revoking credits for legitimate users.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.com | +1 555-204-9981

From: ops@nebulaops.com <ops@nebulaops.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: sales@nebulaops.com
Date: Thu, 01 Jul 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick verification so we can keep your trial credits active

Hi Neha,

Thanks for the note. We are NebulaOps — small infra startup. Attaching a vendor invoice and a screenshot of our G-Suite admin page (we'll send via the Drive link below). Our primary contact is Maya Reynolds, Head of Platform, +1 555-0199.

Drive link: https://drive.google.com/file/d/nebulaops-evidence-sample

Let us know if you need anything else. Happy to join a quick screen-share this afternoon.

— ops@nebulaops.com

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 01 Jul 2027 11:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Suspicious promo credit issuances — NebulaOps cohort

I reviewed the attachments and the Drive evidence link. A few observations:
- The phone number provided (Maya Reynolds, +1 555-0199) exactly matches the number used across many suspect accounts — this is a red flag for reuse/masquerade.
- The invoice PDF appears legitimate but was uploaded from a disposable subdomain on the sender side; cross-check origin headers before trusting.
- Suggested action: rollback the 24 high_confidence_fraud accounts immediately and flag the probable_duplicate_phone group for forced MFA and org-email verification. Open a support ticket with code: SUPPORT-7419 and notify the customer-facing thread once rollback is complete.

If Sales wants to whitelist a specific account for a live demo, require a short recorded screen-share or live verification with the named contact.

Marcus Lin
Security Ops, Redwood Inference
